questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

A household which spends all of its income on bananas and apples makes the following purchases. quantity price per fruit purchased (kg) kg ($) bananas 5 2.50 apples 10 1.00 The household derives twice as much utility from the fifth kg of bananas as from the tenth kg of apples. What should the household do to maximise utility from the purchase of these fruits? purchase of purchase of bananas apples

options.C: no change decrease

questions.questionText: Why will the quantity demanded increase when the price of a normal good falls?

options.A: The income and substitution effects are both positive.
options.B: The income and substitution effects are both negative.
options.C: The negative income effect is greater than the positive substitution effect.
options.D: The positive income effect is greater than the negative substitution effect.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a perfectly competitive firm’s average product of labour and marginal product of labour curves. J K wage ($), labour product (units) M L APL MPL O number employed The market price of the firm’s product is $1. Which segment of the curves represents the firm’s demand for labour curve?

options.A: OJ B JK C KL D KM

questions.questionText: To increase its labour force from 30 to 31 workers, a firm has to increase the daily wage rate from $50 to $52. What is the marginal cost of labour per day?
A trade union seeks to increase the wages a firm pays to its workers while at the same time preserving jobs. What will strengthen the union’s negotiating position?

options.A: Capital and labour are close substitutes.
options.B: The demand for the good produced by the firm is price elastic.
options.C: The supply of labour to the firm is perfectly elastic.
options.D: The firm operates in a monopsonistic labour market.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s short-run total cost curve (TC). TC total cost O Q Q Q
A firm employs three factors of production. The table shows the marginal products of these factors and their respective costs at the current level of output. land labour capital marginal
The diagram shows the cost and revenue curves of a monopoly. MC AC $ MR AR O X output What is the firm’s objective if it produces output OX?

options.C: to maximise total revenue

questions.questionText: The table shows a firm’s total costs corresponding to different levels of output. units of output 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 total cost ($) 8 14 18 22 28 36 46 58 If the market price is $8, within which range of output would a profit maximising firm in a perfectly competitive industry produce in the short run?

options.A: 1 - 2 units B 3 - 4 units C 5 - 6 units D 7 - 8 units

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the cost and revenue curves of a profit-maximising monopolist. ATC MC J revenue, cost K M AR MR O Q output What measures the total monopoly profit made by the firm?

options.A: JM B JK C JM × OQ D JK × OQ

questions.questionText: Some of the firms in an industry agree to set the same price. What might threaten the continuation of the agreement?

options.A: differences in cost structures between firms
options.C: the inclusion of the dominant firm in the industry
options.D: significant barriers to entry into the industry

questions.questionText: What does not pose a threat to the achievement of allocative efficiency?

options.A: imperfect information on the part of consumers
options.C: the existence of externalities

questions.questionText: At present, a monopolist is required by the industry regulator to charge a price equal to marginal cost. The table summarises the consequences if the firm were allowed instead to maximise its profits. $million increase in monopoly profits 5 loss of consumer surplus 8 What would be the resulting deadweight loss?

options.A: $3 million B $5 million C $8 million D $13 million

questions.questionText: The government introduces a congestion charge on motorists who drive their vehicles within a designated urban zone. What will be the impact on the overall economic welfare of those who continue to use their cars and on those who switch to travelling by bus? impact on those who impact on those who continue to use their cars switch to buses

options.C: uncertain loss

questions.questionText: The graphs below show percentage changes in money GDP and consumer prices in a country between 2008 and 2010. % % 2008 2009 2010 2008 2009 2010 % change in % change in money GDP consumer prices Which conclusion may be drawn from the graphs?

options.A: Between 2009 and 2010 money GDP fell but consumer prices continued to rise.
options.B: Consumer prices and money GDP both continued to rise throughout the period.
options.C: In real terms GDP grew throughout the period.
options.D: When consumer prices rose, money GDP fell.

questions.questionText: The table shows data on a country’s gross domestic product (GDP) at market prices and on domestic spending. year 1 year 2 year 3 ($m) ($m) ($m) GDP at market prices 630 650 680 private consumption 460 470 480 government consumption 140 160 170 gross investment 20 30 50 In which of these years will the country be faced with a balance of trade deficit? year 1 year 2 year 3

options.C: no yes yes

questions.questionText: Which row correctly identifies net leakages from the circular flow of income? trade surplus government budget deficit private sector surplus (exports - imports) (government spending - taxes) (saving - investment)

options.C: (cid:2) (cid:1) (cid:1)

questions.questionText: According to monetarist theory, which policy objectives are in conflict in the short run, but not in the long run?

options.C: price stability and equilibrium in the balance of payments

questions.questionText: Let C = consumption, I = investment, X = exports, M = imports, Y = national income in an economy with no government sector. If C = 20 + 0.9Y, I = 60, X = 120 and M = 100, what will be the equilibrium level of Y?
Assuming a constant income velocity of circulation of money, if real output grows by 4%, and the money supply grows by 3%, what will be the approximate change in the price level?
During a recession a government’s expenditure exceeds its tax revenue. Which policy might prevent upward pressure on interest rates?

options.B: purchases of government bonds by the country’s central bank
options.C: sales of foreign currency from the official reserves
options.D: sales of government bonds to the general public

questions.questionText: An economy’s GDP per capita grows over a certain period of time, but its development when measured by the Human Development Index remains unchanged. What could explain the difference?

options.C: increased pollution

questions.questionText: How can cyclical growth, as opposed to long-run economic growth, be shown on a diagram?

options.A: an inward shift in a production possibility curve
options.B: an outward shift in a production possibility curve
options.C: a movement from a point inside a production possibility curve to a point on the curve
options.D: a movement from a point outside a production possibility curve to a point on the curve

questions.questionText: In the long run, productive potential in an economy grows at an average rate of 3 % per year. In a particular year actual growth is zero because of a fall in domestic consumption. What is likely to occur?

options.B: an increase in the rate of inflation
options.C: an increase in the trade deficit
options.D: a reduction in the government budget deficit

questions.questionText: A developing country’s level of debt rises. In which circumstance is this least likely to be a problem?

options.C: The country’s Gross Domestic Product rises by less than its debt.

questions.questionText: The natural rate of unemployment in an economy is 5%. What will happen if a government persists in trying to achieve a target rate of unemployment of 3% by expansionary monetary policy?

options.C: a high but constant rate of inflation

questions.questionText: What is the best measure of the economic cost of an increase in unemployment?

options.B: the money value of the additional social security benefits paid
options.C: the goods and services the unemployed workers could have produced
options.D: the additional social security benefits paid plus the loss of tax revenue from newly redundant workers

questions.questionText: What is the most effective policy a government could introduce to reduce frictional unemployment?

options.C: reduce tax rates

questions.questionText: What is likely to be the effect on developing economies of an increase in inward foreign direct investment?

options.B: an increase in the burden of debt
options.C: an increase in visible trade deficits
